turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come on in and we'll get the measurements done before the doctor sees you. Shoes off for the weight if you don't mind.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah alright. I'm wrecked, can we just get on with it.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Grand. Blood pressure is one oh nine over seventy-seven. Temperature is thirty-eight point three.
[SEG0004] person_1 (NURSE): Weight is fifty-four, ah the scales jumped. It's fifty-two kilos. Last time in March you were sixty-eight. Your last pressure was one-forty.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Pulse now. I'm getting one twenty. No, hang on, let me take that again. It's one twelve.
[SEG0006] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's been restless for weeks at home, hardly sits still.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Doctor will be along in a minute. Have a seat.
[SEG0008] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, this yoke of a computer is after freezing again. Two seconds. Right. What brought you in?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): I'm losing weight and my heart's going mad and I'm sweating the whole time.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, say that again? The file's still coming up.
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Weight's falling off me. Heart racing. Sweating. And my hands shake.
[SEG0012] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She's eating more than usual as well, doctor, not less. I've watched her at the table.
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Mam I can talk. Yeah I'm eating loads and still dropping weight. It's doing my head in.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): How long has the weight been coming off?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, a couple of months. I haven't a notion of the exact date.
[SEG0016] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): After Easter it started. About two months.
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, about two months. Whatever.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Mm. And the racing heart, same length of time?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah it came with the weight. Worse when I'm trying to get to sleep.
[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any chest pain with that?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No. No chest pain.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): Shortness of breath?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): A bit, if I go up the stairs. I'm too tired for them lately.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry, breathless on the stairs? Something just beeped at me.
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, the stairs. And the shaky hands, like I said.
[SEG0026] person_4 (DOCTOR): Are the shakes there all day or do they come and go?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Mostly all day. Worse if I haven't eaten, which is mad because I'm always hungry.
[SEG0028] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She had bloods in the hospital last year. They said it was borderline.
[SEG0029] person_4 (DOCTOR): Borderline what? Can you repeat that, I was in the chart.
[SEG0030] person_2 (PATIENT): Thyroid. They said it was borderline and then nobody did anything.
[SEG0031] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. Any thyroid problems in the family?
[SEG0032] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Her sister Aoife has an overactive thyroid. On tablets for years.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah Aoife. That's why mam hauled me in here.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): What medicines are you on at the minute?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Just the Crocin when a headache hits. Two of them.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): Crocin, the paracetemol? How often?
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Few times a week. And the GP gave me a water tablet ages ago. I stopped it, had me running to the loo.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): The name of that water tablet?
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't remember. Little white ones. Took them a week and packed them in.
[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any allergies?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): No. None.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): Do you smoke?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Never.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alcohol?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): A few pints at the weekend. Hardly even that now, I'm too wrecked.
[SEG0046] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): She lives with me. I do the dinners, she hasn't the energy to cook.
[SEG0047] person_4 (DOCTOR): Hands out for me. There's a fine tremor there. Pulse is rapid, matches the nurse. Neck doesn't look swollen.
[SEG0048] person_2 (PATIENT): So it's the thyroid, is it.

[SEG0049] person_4 (DOCTOR): Could be an overactive thyroid, that's my working impression, but I'm not calling it until the bloods are back. We'll do thyroid bloods today and an ECG for the fast heart.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): Today? I've work to get back to.

[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): Both are booked for this afternoon downstairs, won't take long. Come back here in two weeks for the results. If the racing heart comes with chest pain before then, go to the emergency department, don't wait on me.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Fine. Two weeks. Can we go now.

spec.situation: Younger adult losing weight with a fast heartbeat, sweating, shaky hands, eats more than usual; hair thinning not mentioned; a sister has thyroid disease; blood tests and ECG planned.

traps.happens: The nurse reads vital signs aloud in spoken words ('one oh nine over seventy-seven', 'thirty-eight point three') and also gives a PRIOR value ('last time in March you were sixty-eight', 'your last pressure was one-forty'). Someone may also correct a reading.
traps.label_rule: vital_signs hold only the CURRENT measured values, written normally (109/77, 38.3, 52 kg). The prior value is NOT a vital sign; it is recorded in the weight/BP entry's own notes only if the schema allows, otherwise omitted. Every number must be exactly as said; never invent or round a value that was not said.

features: test_result_recalled: the patient reports an old test or result ('they said it was borderline'); recorded as reported history/investigation only as far as said, not as a confirmed value.

colloquial_drug_names: medicines referred to by colour, purpose or brand ('the water tablet', 'Crocin', 'my sugar tablets', 'the purple inhaler'); the name is recorded as said, the normalized name only if it is clear.
spec.doctor_style: distracted by the computer, asks for repeats

bad.reason: Doctor says thyroid bloods will be done today; not completed or requested by patient.

omissions.text: Weight loss quantified by nurse: last weight in March was 68 kg, now 52 kg.
Breathlessness was described as only 'a bit' and specifically on exertion climbing stairs.
Shaky hands/tremor are worse if she has not eaten.
Past history from patient/family: hospital blood tests last year reportedly showed 'borderline' thyroid.
Discontinued water tablet caused urinary frequency/'had me running to the loo' as reason for stopping.
Doctor stated he is not confirming overactive thyroid until blood results are back.
Investigations were booked downstairs for this afternoon and doctor said they would not take long.
Recorded investigation fact is wrong: the thyroid blood test was not completed and was not requested by the patient; it was planned/requested by the doctor for later that day.
